target_customer: Managers of labor-intensive factories with many workers on production lines, mainly mid-size manufacturers in Germany
problem: Factories with many manual workers cannot see what happens on the line, so downtime, quality issues and productivity losses go unnoticed. Enterprise manufacturing execution systems cost millions to set up and run.
business_model: B2B SaaS plus hardware terminals (touchscreen terminals with RFID readers at each workstation)
product_category: Manufacturing execution and production tracking software

founders.name: Sascha Lang
founders.background_notes: YC page: industrial engineer with 15+ years in factories and on production sites as project and sales manager. No named employers or school on the page.

competitors.name: Retrocausal
competitors.what: AI software that analyzes manual assembly work from video to improve line productivity and quality
competitors.traction_then: Shipping Retroactivity quality control software in late 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: Terminals with RFID readers, dashboards, alerts and photo based quality checks are standard embedded and web engineering. No research grade problem is described on the company site.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware installed at each workstation and accumulated line data create some switching cost, but nothing on the site points to proprietary technology or a network effect.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The company site contrasts itself with unnamed enterprise manufacturing execution systems. No source shows an incumbent copying or buying it.

market_need_then: The company site argues that enterprise MES costs millions to set up and run, leaving labor-intensive mid-size factories without affordable production tracking. No independent demand data was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses aisupervision.com per the YC page; no acquisition history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain functional language on the site ('what the best human supervisor would do')

brand_strength.rationale: No press, community or brand story found; searches returned only database profiles. The name is descriptive and shared with generic AI supervision products.

outcome_analysis: AiSupervision sold production tracking software and hardware to labor-intensive factories from Mannheim and raised about 500 thousand dollars around its Winter 2022 batch. The YC directory marks it Inactive, but no shutdown, insolvency or acquisition report was found, and CB Insights still lists it as alive, so the cause of inactivity is not public. With one named founder and little public traction data, no failure factor can be supported.
notes: The 500K round rests on CB Insights (labeled Seed VC, March 29 2022) and Seedtable (labeled Pre Seed with 0M); stage label conflicts, so pre_seed follows Seedtable. A single database reports it. The CB Insights page said founded 2020 and Alive; the YC directory says Inactive. Company site names no founders and no competitors. Drishti was found but no source dated near the batch, so it is not listed. Founder education and employers not found.
